title: Where Optional belongs, and what a lambda can capture

questions.stem: Per this page, in which role is `Optional` meant to appear?

options.text: As a method's return type, when a result may be absent
options.says: The page says Optional is designed for return types, not for fields, parameters, or collections.

options.text: As a field's type, when a value may be left unset
options.says: The page names fields among the places Optional is not designed for.

options.text: As a parameter's type, when an argument may be left out
options.says: The page names method parameters among the places Optional is not designed for.

questions.stem: A method declares `int count = 0;` and then calls `list.forEach(item -> count++);`. Per this page, what happens?

options.text: It runs, and count ends equal to the list's size
options.says: The page marks this code as a compilation error, so it never runs: lambdas can only access effectively final local variables.

options.text: It runs, but count is still 0 after the loop
options.says: No copy of count is updated either: the page says the line does not compile, because count is not effectively final.

options.text: It does not compile, since count is changed
options.says: The page shows it as a compilation error: a lambda can only access local variables that are effectively final.
